The **Super Bowl LVIII halftime show** , officially known as the **[Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") Super Bowl LVIII Halftime Show**, was the [halftime entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halftime_show "Halftime show") of [Super Bowl LVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII"), which took place on February 11, 2024, at [Allegiant Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allegiant_Stadium "Allegiant Stadium") in [Paradise, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-1) It featured [Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_\(musician\) "Usher \(musician\)") as the headline performer, with guest appearances by [Alicia Keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Keys "Alicia Keys"), [will.i.am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will.i.am "Will.i.am"), [Lil Jon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Jon "Lil Jon"), [Ludacris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludacris "Ludacris"), [H.E.R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.E.R. "H.E.R."), and [Sonic Boom of the South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic_Boom_of_the_South "Sonic Boom of the South").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-2) The show was televised nationally by [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL_on_CBS "NFL on CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") and the Apple Music app.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-3) The television broadcast was watched by 129 million viewers in the US, making it the third most watched halftime show in history.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-4)
## Background
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]
### Artists in contention to headline the halftime show
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Artists in contention to headline the halftime show")]
Throughout summer 2023, there were various names being reported to be performing at the halftime show, including former [One Direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Direction "One Direction") member and British singer [Harry Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Styles "Harry Styles") to promote his recent album _[Harry's House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry's_House "Harry's House")_ , which won the [Album of the Year Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year") at the [2023 Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/65th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "65th Annual Grammy Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-5) [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift") was reportedly considered for the show; she later pulled out of the running due to having prior commitments such as her [Eras Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Eras_Tour "The Eras Tour"), which was reported by _[Cosmopolitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmopolitan_\(magazine\) "Cosmopolitan \(magazine\)")_ in August 2023.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-6) Still, Swift was in attendance,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-i105-7) leading to speculation that [her popularity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_impact_of_Taylor_Swift "Cultural impact of Taylor Swift") helped cause the actual football game (and the halftime show as a carryover) to become to the most-viewed television broadcast in modern history. [Miley Cyrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miley_Cyrus "Miley Cyrus") was another artist also being considered to headline the show.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-8) Other rumored artists included [Bad Bunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Bunny "Bad Bunny"), [Jack Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Harlow "Jack Harlow"), and [NSYNC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSYNC "NSYNC").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-9) Usher was informed of his selection on August 11, 2023.
### Headliner announcement
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Headliner announcement")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fa/Usher_Cannes_2016_retusche.jpg/250px-Usher_Cannes_2016_retusche.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Usher_Cannes_2016_retusche.jpg)[Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_\(musician\) "Usher \(musician\)") headlined the halftime show as part of [Super Bowl LVIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII "Super Bowl LVIII") on February 11, 2024, two days after the release date of his ninth studio album _[Coming Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_Home_\(Usher_album\) "Coming Home \(Usher album\)")_.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-:0-10)
On September 24, 2023, it was announced that Usher would headline the show with this being his second appearance at a halftime show following the [Super Bowl XLV halftime show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLV_halftime_show "Super Bowl XLV halftime show") which was headlined by American musical group the [Black Eyed Peas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Eyed_Peas "Black Eyed Peas") where he was a guest alongside [Slash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slash_\(musician\) "Slash \(musician\)"), making Raymond the first act to perform during both a Super Bowl and an [NBA Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_Finals "2015 NBA Finals"). He had been reported to be a potential headliner for a while after extending his residency at the [MGM Grand Garden Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MGM_Grand_Garden_Arena "MGM Grand Garden Arena").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-11) His participation is the latest result of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League") (NFL)'s partnership with [Jay Z](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Z "Jay Z")'s entertainment agency [Roc Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roc_Nation "Roc Nation"), which was signed in 2019 to boost the quality of the halftime shows. Coincidentally, Usher marked his thirtieth anniversary as a solo artist (1994–2024),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-12) and the lead-up to his headlining prominently made note of that fact. After his announcement as the headliner, he said: "It's a honor of a lifetime to finally check a Super Bowl performance off my bucket list. I can't wait to bring the world a show unlike anything else they've seen from me before". Speaking to [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music")'s [Zane Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zane_Lowe "Zane Lowe") on potential guests, he said, "Well, one thing I can say is that I have collaborated with a lot of incredible artists throughout the years," including fellow singers and rappers [Alicia Keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Keys "Alicia Keys"), [will.i.am](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will.i.am "Will.i.am"), [Lil Jon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lil_Jon "Lil Jon"), [Ludacris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludacris "Ludacris"), and [H.E.R.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.E.R. "H.E.R.") playing guitar. As a nod to [Black History Month](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_History_Month "Black History Month"), the [HBCU](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBCU "HBCU") marching band [Sonic Boom of the South](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonic_Boom_of_the_South "Sonic Boom of the South") played on-field brass and percussion.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-:0-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-14)
### Alicia Keys' vocal gaffe
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Alicia Keys' vocal gaffe")]
[Alicia Keys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alicia_Keys "Alicia Keys")' voice cracked at the beginning of her performance of "[If I Ain't Got You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If_I_Ain't_Got_You "If I Ain't Got You")". In the [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") upload of the halftime show, the [NFL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NFL "NFL") scrubbed the mistake[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-15) by editing in the correct notes from a prior rehearsal performance to fix Keys' off-key and pitchy vocals.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-18)
## Reception
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Reception")]
In a four-star review, Adrian Horton of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")_ described the performance "frenetic and daring" while "at times chaotic and uncharacteristically wobbly".[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-19) Dominic Patten of _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ wrote "as tight as the tone and pacing of the performance was, Usher felt very 20 years ago and flat," compared to the previous two shows and [Andra Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andra_Day "Andra Day")'s "[Lift Every Voice and Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_Every_Voice_and_Sing "Lift Every Voice and Sing")" performance.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-20)
This was the 32nd edition of the Super Bowl Halftime Show, and topped out with 129.3 million concurrent viewers, making it the biggest television audience in its history since the [inaugural show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_XXVII_halftime_show "Super Bowl XXVII halftime show") featuring [Michael Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jackson "Michael Jackson") (133.4 million).[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-21)
Usher's album, _[Coming Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_Home_\(Usher_album\) "Coming Home \(Usher album\)")_ , was propelled to No. 2 on the Billboard 200 charts upon its debut the following week with 91,000 [units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") moved.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-22) The record held the #1 slot on [iTunes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITunes "ITunes") the week leading up the big game.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LVIII_halftime_show#cite_note-e741-23)
The show was nominated for [Outstanding Variety Special (Live)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Variety_Special_\(Live\) "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Variety Special \(Live\)"), [Outstanding Lighting Design / Lighting Direction for a Variety Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Lighting_Design_/_Lighting_Direction_for_a_Variety_Special "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lighting Design / Lighting Direction for a Variety Special") and [Outstanding Technical Direction and Camerawork for a Special](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Technical_Direction_and_Camerawork_for_a_Special "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Technical Direction and Camerawork for a Special") at the [76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/76th_Primetime_Creative_Arts_Emmy_Awards "76th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards").
